sections.title: Repetition, Unhurried Pace, and Emotional Warmth
sections.content: The productive derivational suffix -gat/-get (attached directly after vowel stems or via a linking vowel -ogat/-eget/-öget after consonant clusters and many monosyllables) modifies the aspect of a Hungarian verb in two closely related ways: (1) Iterative/Frequentative: performing an action repeatedly in small increments (kérdezget 'keeps asking questions', rakosgat 'arranges piece by piece'); (2) Attenuative/Leisurely: doing something casually, unhurriedly, or for pleasure without pressure to finish (olvasgat 'reads at leisure', nézeget 'browses / looks over fondly').

sections.title: Transitivity and Preverb Behavior
sections.content: Frequentative verbs in -gat/-get retain the transitivity and conjugation rules of their base verb (olvasgat egy könyvet -> olvasgatja a régi leveleket). When combined with a preverb such as meg- or át-, the meaning becomes 'do a little bit / do repeatedly with care': megvereget ('pats gently several times'), átlapozgat ('flips through casually').

sections.title: Base Verb vs. Frequentative -gat/-get
rows: Esténként a nagyapám régi naplóját olvasgatom.
Sokáig nézegettük a megsárgult családi fényképeket.
A gyerekek kíváncsian kérdezgették a pásztort.
Ábel gondosan rakosgatta a tűzifát a kunyhó mellett.

items.spanish: A téli estéken a tűzhely mellett ültünk, és régi kalendáriumokat lapozgattunk.
items.english: On winter evenings we sat by the hearth and leafed casually through old almanacs.

items.spanish: Az édesapja elismerően megveregette a fiú vállát a nehéz munka után.
items.english: His father approvingly patted the boy's shoulder after the hard work.

items.spanish: A nagymama órákig rendezgette a padláson talált emlékeket.
items.english: Grandmother spent hours lovingly arranging the keepsakes found in the attic.

items.spanish: Csak ízlelgette a székely szavakat, mintha régi dallamot hallgatna.
items.english: He was just savoring the Székely words as if listening to an old melody.

sections.title: B2 Stylistic Notice
sections.content: Be careful not to confuse frequentative -gat/-get with causative -tat/-tet: 'olvasgat' means 'he reads casually for himself', whereas 'olvastat' means 'he makes someone else read'.
